title: Prepay, contest or appeal a traffic ticket
question: I got a traffic ticket in Staunton. Can I prepay it, how do I contest it, and what if I cannot pay?
office: Staunton General District Court, Clerk's Office (25th Judicial District)
summary: Tickets written in Staunton normally go to the Staunton General District Court; use the court named on the summons. If the offence is on the Uniform Fine Schedule, you can prepay online (4% card fee; by 3:30 pm the business day before trial), by mail (it must arrive before the court date) or at the Clerk's Office. Prepaying is a guilty plea reported to DMV. Reckless driving (including 20 mph or more over the limit, or over 85 mph), DUI, driving suspended or unlicensed, leaving the scene and indictable offences cannot be prepaid. To contest, appear on the summons date; a judge decides without a jury, and the clerk can grant a first continuance. If you cannot pay in full, the court must offer a payment plan, and community service can earn credit. You can appeal to the Staunton Circuit Court within 10 days, with a jury there.

steps.step: Find out which court has the ticket
steps.who: Person charged (the driver named on the summons)
steps.how: The court is named at the top of the summons. A ticket written in the City of Staunton is normally returnable to the Staunton General District Court, 113 E. Beverley St.; always use the court named on your summons. A ticket written in surrounding Augusta County normally goes to the separate Augusta General District Court in Verona, which is in the same 25th Judicial District. Read the NOTICE on the back of the summons and the charge after DESCRIBE CHARGE on the front. If you lost the ticket or do not know which court it went to, search your name in the statewide Online Case Information System (it cannot take payments).
steps.deadline: Before the court date on the summons
steps.quote: If you have lost your traffic ticket (summons) or do not know the jurisdiction in which the summons was issued, you may use the Online Case Information System-Statewide Search to search statewide using your name; however, payments cannot be made using this system.

steps.step: Check whether the offence can be prepaid
steps.how: Only offences listed in the Supreme Court's Uniform Fine Schedule (Rule 3B:2), whether charged under the state statute or a parallel city ordinance, can be prepaid; every other traffic offence needs a court hearing. Staunton's City Code adopts the state motor vehicle law (Title 46.2) by reference, except provisions whose violation is a felony or a Class 1 or 2 misdemeanour, so a city traffic infraction normally parallels a state one. State law bars prepaying indictable offences, driving under the influence, reckless driving, leaving the scene of an accident, driving while suspended or revoked, and driving without a licence. Speeding 20 mph or more over the limit, or over 85 mph, is reckless driving, so it cannot be prepaid. A city ordinance with no state parallel can be prepaid only if it appears on a schedule entered by the circuit court; none was found for Staunton. If the officer gave you a Virginia Prepayable Offenses Information Sheet, look for your charge in its table. If it is not there, or you got no sheet, call the court for instructions.
steps.quote: For traffic offenses not listed below, a court hearing is required.

steps.step: Decide whether to prepay or to go to court
steps.how: Prepaying is a written guilty plea: you give up the trial, your signed plea has the force of a court judgment, and the conviction is sent to DMV, which may assess demerit points. To contest the charge, do not prepay; appear in court on the summons date (step s9).
steps.quote: Pre-court payments are deemed a waiver of a court hearing and entry of a guilty plea.

steps.step: Work out the amount to prepay
steps.how: The amount is the fine on the Uniform Fine Schedule plus court costs. The schedule sets the same fine everywhere in Virginia (for example, speeding is $6 per mph over the limit, $7 per mph in a school crossing or highway work zone, and $200 plus $8 per mph in a residence district) and adds the $51 fixed fee for a traffic infraction. Other costs set by statute are added on top. Several charges from one incident carry the fixed fee once for a single appearance, and the court cannot waive costs. Staunton's City Code (§ 3.05.080) assesses $2 for courthouse maintenance and $5 for the electronic summons system in each traffic case, and $20 for courthouse security on conviction; under state law the $5 applies only to tickets written by a local law-enforcement agency. No Staunton General District Court fee sheet was found, so check the total in the online system or call the court.
steps.fee: The fine on the Uniform Fine Schedule plus costs, including the $51 fixed fee for a traffic infraction and Staunton's local assessments (see fees)
steps.quote: This schedule is applied uniformly throughout the Commonwealth, and a clerk or magistrate may not impose a fine different from the amounts shown here.

steps.who: Person charged, paying the Staunton General District Court
steps.how: Open the General District Court Online Case Information System and choose Staunton General District Court (the court named on the summons). Search by name, case number or hearing date. If the case shows Mark For Payment, mark it (up to five cases on one receipt), choose Process Payment, pay by credit or debit card, and print the confirmation screen as your receipt. Payments made after 3:30 pm (Eastern Time) are processed the next business day. For a refund, contact the court that took the payment.
steps.deadline: Before 3:30 pm on the business day before the trial date
steps.fee: Fine and costs, plus a 4% card convenience fee per transaction
steps.quote: Payment must be made prior to 3:30 pm on the business day before the trial date to ensure the payment will be processed before the court date.

steps.how: Follow the PRETRIAL WAIVER AND PREPAYMENT INSTRUCTIONS on the summons and mail the payment to the court named on it: Staunton General District Court, 113 E. Beverley St., 1st Floor, Staunton, VA 24401-4390 (the address on the court's vacourts.gov page; use the address on your summons if it differs). District courts accept personal checks, money orders, certified checks and credit cards; make a check payable to the court (presumably Staunton General District Court; the state page's example is a county general district court's name). For a card, fill in the Credit Card Authorization on the back of the prepayable offenses sheet, and confirm with the court which cards it takes. The payment counts only when the court receives it, and a further fee is added if it arrives after the court date. Do not mail it to the Office of the Executive Secretary of the Supreme Court.
steps.deadline: It must reach the court before the court date (payment counts on receipt, not on mailing); the state page advises mailing at least 7 days before the court date
steps.quote: Prepayment of the fine(s) and fee(s) is effective only upon receipt by the applicable general district court, not on the date that you mail it.

steps.who: Person charged, at the Staunton General District Court Clerk's Office (or before a magistrate)
steps.how: Go to the Clerk's Office at 113 E. Beverley St., 1st Floor, Staunton, during office hours (8:30 am to 4:30 pm). Cell phones are not allowed in the building. State law requires district courts to accept personal checks and credit or debit cards, but the clerk may refuse them on listed grounds (for example, an earlier dishonoured check or a card payment that is not authorised), and the clerk may add a card convenience fee of up to 4% or a flat fee of up to $2. State law also lets you make the written appearance in person before a magistrate before the trial date.
steps.fee: Fine and costs; the clerk may add a card convenience fee of up to 4% or a flat fee of up to $2
steps.quote: An appearance may be made in person or in writing by mail to a clerk of court or in person before a magistrate, prior to any date fixed for trial in court.

steps.step: If you need a new court date, ask for a continuance
steps.who: Person charged, to the Clerk's Office; a judge decides later requests
steps.how: The court's clerk can grant a first continuance; any later request goes to a judge by motion. Give your reason; a judge does not have to grant a request. Once a continuance is granted in advance of the trial date, Form DC-344 lets you promise in writing, sworn before a judge, clerk, deputy clerk or notary, to appear on the new date, so the court will not require you to appear on the original date (it may still require that if you are in violation of pretrial release terms or have missed a court date before). The form's instructions send its first copy to the attorney for the Commonwealth, and its certificate records that delivery.
steps.quote: First continuance granted by Clerk; subsequent requests by Judge on motion.

steps.step: To contest the ticket, go to trial on the court date
steps.who: Person charged; a Staunton General District Court judge decides
steps.how: Appear at the Staunton General District Court at the date and time on the summons. The court hears traffic and criminal cases every Wednesday, the 5th Thursday, and the 1st, 3rd and 5th Fridays (excluding holidays): arraignments and advisements at 9:00 am, traffic infractions and non-contested criminal cases at 9:30 am, and trials and contested cases at 10:30 am. Cell phones are not allowed in the building. A judge decides the case without a jury (state law requires this for a traffic infraction, and the general district court holds no jury trials), and you are presumed innocent until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt. You can plead guilty, not guilty or nolo contendere, and you can hire a lawyer. You can have the clerk's office subpoena your witnesses; Form DC-325 advises filing the request at least ten days before trial. The fine schedule does not limit the fine the judge can set after a hearing.
steps.deadline: The court date on the summons; Form DC-325 advises requesting witness subpoenas at least ten days before trial
steps.fee: If found guilty: the fine the judge sets plus costs, including the $51 fixed fee for a traffic infraction ($61 for a misdemeanour such as reckless driving)

steps.step: If the charge could carry jail time and you cannot afford a lawyer, ask for one
steps.how: Some traffic charges are misdemeanours that can carry up to a year in jail (for example, reckless driving, a Class 1 misdemeanour, or driving while suspended). If you cannot afford a lawyer, tell the court; the judge examines your finances, usually from your sworn financial statement on Form DC-333, and may appoint a lawyer. The cost of an appointed lawyer is added to your costs if you are found guilty. Traffic infractions punishable only by a fine do not qualify.
steps.deadline: Before or at the first court date
steps.quote: If the accused shall claim that he is indigent, and the charge against him is a criminal offense that may be punishable by confinement in the state correctional facility or jail

steps.step: If you need a disability accommodation, ask the clerk
steps.who: Person charged (or a witness), to the Staunton General District Court Clerk's Office
steps.how: Ask the Clerk's Office for the aid or change you need before the court date. Virginia's courts generally provide, on request, aids and services such as qualified interpreters for people with speech, hearing or vision impairments, at no surcharge.
steps.quote: A request for accommodation should be made to the relevant clerk if the request relates to a pending case or activity of a particular court.

steps.step: Know what happens if you neither prepay nor appear
steps.how: For a traffic infraction, if you neither prepay nor appear, you are treated as having waived a hearing: the case may be heard without you, you are notified of the finding, and the court may not issue a failure-to-appear warrant under Va. Code § 46.2-938. A $35 failure-to-appear cost is added unless you ask for a hearing and show good cause. In criminal cases (including misdemeanour traffic charges such as reckless driving) and certain other traffic cases, a separate warrant may be issued on a new charge of failure to appear, and you would stand trial on that charge as well as the original one.
steps.fee: $35 added to costs when you fail to appear, unless you request a hearing and show good cause
steps.quote: In criminal and certain traffic cases, if you fail to pre-pay the fine and costs (when allowed) and also fail to appear in court, a separate warrant may be issued against you on a new charge of failure to appear.

steps.step: After a conviction, pay or ask for a payment agreement
steps.who: Person convicted, at the Staunton General District Court Clerk's Office (the clerk or a deputy clerk approves)
steps.how: The court must tell you in writing about payment agreements and must offer you one. Under the 25th Judicial District's policy, if you cannot pay in full within 90 days of conviction, ask the Clerk's Office for an installment agreement (monthly payments in the amount set when you sign), a deferred agreement (pay everything at the end) or a modified deferred agreement (pay at the end, making best efforts to pay monthly in between). A deferred or modified deferred agreement must be paid in full within 6 to 12 months, as the clerk sets it. State law lets the court offer installments of $25 a month or more depending on your ability to pay, or less if it finds you indigent. The court may not require a down payment on a first agreement (you may make one voluntarily). The court may ask for a sworn financial statement; Form DC-211 is the state petition for an agreement. Tell the court if you receive Social Security or SSI: under the policy no payment can be taken from those benefits, and if they are your sole financial resource, state law exempts you from making payments and bars sending the case to collection.
steps.deadline: Pay in full within 90 days of conviction or enter a payment agreement (the court must offer one); under an agreement, a payment received within 10 days of its due date is on time
steps.fee: No plan fee is stated in the 25th District policy; state law allows a one-time fee of up to $10 (see fees)
steps.quote: Any defendant who is unable to pay in full the fines and costs for a particular offense within 90 days of conviction, or for any other disposition authorized by law, shall be offered the opportunity to enter into an Installment Plan Agreement, Deferred Payment Agreement, or Deferred Modified Agreement

steps.step: Or work off fines and costs with community service
steps.who: Person convicted, with the court's approval
steps.how: Ask the court to approve community service. The work is done at a nonprofit, whose supervisor signs documentation that you give to the court. Each hour is credited at the state minimum wage, and at least 15 hours a month are required unless the court sets fewer for good cause. Community service cannot be credited against restitution, interest on restitution, or any collection fee. The Clerk may grant one extension of up to 6 months if your written request reaches the Clerk before the due date for completion.
steps.deadline: At least 15 hours a month; extension requests in writing before the due date for completion
steps.quote: A defendant shall be permitted to discharge all or part of the fines and costs owed by performing community service.

steps.step: If you cannot keep up with the agreement, ask to change it before you default
steps.who: Person on a payment agreement, in writing to the Clerk; the court decides
steps.how: Write to the Clerk asking to change the agreement (Form DC-211 is the state form for a modification request). Under the policy the request must come before you miss a payment. On an installment agreement you may petition the court to lower the monthly payment for good cause; on a deferred agreement, write to the Clerk for an extension before the due date. Under the policy, default means not paying as agreed or not doing the agreed community service. If you do default, the clerk removes you from the agreement, but you can petition the court for a new one; the court may require a down payment, which state law caps.
steps.deadline: Before any default in payments (deferred agreements: before the due date)
steps.fee: Down payment on a subsequent agreement, capped by Va. Code § 19.2-354.1(I) (see fees)
steps.quote: Modification requests may be submitted to the Clerk in writing any time during the duration of the Payment Agreement, and the Court may grant such modification based on need.

steps.step: Pay later online or by mail, before the account goes to collection
steps.how: Online, in the same General District Court system, from 6:00 am the day after the trial (not on the trial date). By mail, call the court for the amount and your reference case number, write the number on your check (personal check, money order or certified check), and mail it to the court where the case was heard. Online payments carry the 4% card fee. Without a payment agreement, an unpaid balance is sent to collection 90 days after the court date. The state page says interest accrues 181 days after the court date (state law bars interest for 180 days after the final judgment, then charges the judgment rate); no interest accrues while you pay under a court payment agreement.
steps.deadline: Within 90 days of the court date, unless you have a payment agreement
steps.fee: Interest at the judgment rate after 180 days if unpaid; 4% card fee online (see fees)
steps.quote: If you have not entered into a “time to pay” or deferred payment agreement and the court has not received your payment within 90 days following your court date, your account will be sent to collection.

steps.step: Appeal a conviction to the Staunton Circuit Court
steps.who: Person convicted, by notice to the Staunton General District Court clerk; the Staunton Circuit Court hears the appeal
steps.how: File a notice of appeal with the General District Court clerk within ten days of the conviction, whatever your plea. The Staunton Circuit Court (113 East Beverley Street; Clerk's Office on the third floor) tries the case again from the start, and you have the right to a jury, including on a traffic infraction; check with the Circuit Court clerk about scheduling one. Its terms begin on the third Monday of January, April, July and October. No new bond is required. You can withdraw the appeal before it is heard and pay the fine and costs, by written notice to the court and the prosecution before the hearing date. A withdrawal within ten days of the conviction adds no costs; after ten days the Circuit Court affirms the judgment and its clerk taxes the costs. The court does not forward the conviction abstract to DMV until the appeal period has passed with no appeal perfected.
steps.deadline: Within ten days of the conviction
steps.quote: If you wish to appeal your case to the circuit court, you must file a notice of appeal with the clerk of the general district court within ten days of the judgment or conviction by the general district court.

fees.item: Fixed fee for a misdemeanour in district court, for example reckless driving (part of the costs)
fees.quote: In misdemeanors tried in district court, except for those proceedings provided for in subsection C, there shall be assessed as court costs a fixed fee of $61.

fees.amount: $20.00 per conviction in each criminal or traffic case (Staunton City Code § 3.05.080(2), paraphrased; state cap $20)
fees.quote: Any county or city, through its governing body, may assess a sum not in excess of $20 as part of the costs in each criminal or traffic case in its district or circuit court in which the defendant is convicted of a violation of any statute or ordinance.

fees.amount: $2.00 in each criminal or traffic case in which the defendant is charged (Staunton City Code § 3.05.080(1), paraphrased; state cap $2)
fees.quote: Any county or city, through its governing body, may assess a sum not in excess of two dollars as part of the costs in (i) each civil action filed in the district or circuit courts located within its boundaries and (ii) each criminal or traffic case in its district or circuit court in which the defendant is charged with a violation of any statute or ordinance.

fees.amount: $5.00 in each criminal or traffic case in which the defendant is charged (Staunton City Code § 3.05.080(4), paraphrased; state law limits it to charges brought by a local law-enforcement agency; cap $5)
fees.quote: Any county, city, or town, through its governing body, may assess an additional sum not in excess of $5 as part of the costs in each criminal or traffic case in the district or circuit courts located where such cases are brought in which the defendant is charged with a violation of any statute or ordinance

fees.amount: $35, unless good cause is shown at a hearing you request
fees.quote: a fee of $35 shall be taxed as costs whenever a defendant fails to appear, unless, after a hearing requested by such person, good cause is shown for such failure to appear.

fees.item: Credit or debit card convenience fee (online, before or after court)
fees.amount: 4% per transaction (state law caps a card fee at 4% or a flat $2)
fees.quote: There is a 4% convenience fee assessed per transaction when payment is made by credit/debit card.

fees.item: Mailed prepayment received after the court date
fees.quote: An additional fee will be added if payment is received after the court date.

fees.amount: Not stated in the 25th District policy; state law allows a one-time fee of up to $10 if you cannot pay within 90 days of sentencing
fees.quote: If the defendant is unable to make payment within 90 days of sentencing, the court may assess a one-time fee not to exceed $10 to cover the costs of management of the defendant's account until such account is paid in full.

fees.item: Down payment on a subsequent payment agreement (after a default)
fees.amount: Set by the court from the remaining balance (25th District policy), capped at 10% if $500 or less owed; otherwise 5% or $50, whichever is greater
fees.quote: provided that the down payment required to enter into a subsequent payment agreement shall not exceed (i) if the fines and costs owed are $500 or less, 10 percent of such amount or (ii) if the fines and costs owed are more than $500, five percent of such amount or $50, whichever is greater.

fees.item: Interest on unpaid fines and costs
fees.amount: None for 180 days after the judgment, and none while you pay under a court payment agreement; then the judgment rate
fees.quote: No interest shall accrue on any fine or costs imposed in a criminal case or in a case involving a traffic infraction (i) for a period of 180 days following the date of the final judgment imposing such fine or costs;

fees.item: Returned check or refused card payment
fees.amount: The clerk may impose $50 or 10% of the payment, whichever is greater
fees.quote: may impose a fee of $50 or 10 percent of the value of the payment, whichever is greater, in addition to the fine and costs already imposed.

escalation.trigger: The clerk will not grant a continuance, or a second or later continuance is needed
escalation.next: A Staunton General District Court judge, on motion
escalation.basis: Staunton General District Court continuance policy (https://www.vacourts.gov/courts/gd/staunton/home)
escalation.quote: First continuance granted by Clerk; subsequent requests by Judge on motion.

escalation.trigger: Cannot pay the fine and costs in full, or the Clerk's Office will not set up or answer a request for a payment agreement
escalation.next: Staunton General District Court (judge), by petition on Form DC-211
escalation.quote: The court shall offer any defendant the opportunity to enter into a deferred payment agreement, modified deferred payment agreement, or installment payment agreement.

escalation.trigger: Refused a payment agreement because of the offence, the amount owed, or an earlier default
escalation.next: Staunton General District Court (judge), raising the statutory bar on those grounds
escalation.quote: The court shall not deny a defendant the opportunity to enter into a deferred, modified deferred, or installment payment agreement solely (i) because of the category of offense for which the defendant was convicted or found not innocent, (ii) because of the total amount of all fines and costs, (iii) because the defendant previously defaulted under the terms of a payment agreement

escalation.trigger: Asked for a down payment on a first payment agreement
escalation.next: Staunton General District Court (judge), raising the statutory bar on down payments
escalation.quote: No court shall require a defendant to make a down payment upon entering a deferred, modified deferred, or installment payment agreement, other than a subsequent payment agreement

escalation.trigger: Asked to pay, or the account is sent to collection, although your sole financial resource is Social Security or SSI
escalation.next: Staunton General District Court (clerk, then judge): tell the court the benefit is your sole financial resource (Form DC-211's request to modify has a box for this)
escalation.quote: If such defendant informs the court that his sole financial resource is a Social Security benefit or Supplemental Security Income, the case shall not be referred to collections pursuant to § 19.2-349 .

escalation.trigger: Circumstances change during a payment agreement
escalation.next: Staunton General District Court, written request to the Clerk (Form DC-211) to modify the agreement
escalation.deadline: Before any default in payments (25th District policy)
escalation.quote: At any time during the duration of a payment agreement, the defendant may request a modification of the agreement in writing on a form provided by the Executive Secretary of the Supreme Court, and the court may grant such modification based on a good faith showing of need.

escalation.trigger: Defaulted on a payment agreement and removed from it
escalation.next: Staunton General District Court, petition for a subsequent payment agreement (down payment capped by statute)
escalation.quote: A defendant who has defaulted on a payment agreement may petition the court for a subsequent payment agreement.

escalation.trigger: Ordered to show cause for not paying
escalation.next: Staunton General District Court show-cause hearing (the court can allow more time, lower the payments or remit the unpaid amount if the default is excusable)
escalation.quote: the court may enter an order allowing the defendant additional time for payment, reducing the amount due or of each installment, or remitting the unpaid portion in whole or in part.

escalation.trigger: Tried in absence and charged the $35 failure-to-appear cost
escalation.next: Staunton General District Court, hearing requested by the defendant to show good cause
escalation.quote: a fee of $35 shall be taxed as costs whenever a defendant fails to appear, unless, after a hearing requested by such person, good cause is shown for such failure to appear.

escalation.trigger: Convicted in the General District Court (after trial, in absence, or on a guilty plea)
escalation.next: Staunton Circuit Court: new trial from the start (de novo, Va. Code § 16.1-136), with a jury available
escalation.deadline: Within ten days from the conviction
escalation.quote: Any person convicted in a district court of an offense not felonious shall have the right, at any time within ten days from such conviction, and whether or not such conviction was upon a plea of guilty, to appeal to the circuit court.

escalation.trigger: Convicted again in the Circuit Court
escalation.quote: Any aggrieved party may appeal to the Court of Appeals from any final conviction in a circuit court of a traffic infraction or a crime.

caveats: The City of Staunton's website (www.ci.staunton.va.us) refuses automated readers, and no city page is relied on here. The court facts come from the courts' own pages and PDFs on vacourts.gov.

City Code. Staunton's code is on General Code's eCode360, whose terms limit content to personal use and forbid reproducing it for public purposes, so no City Code text is quoted. The paraphrases here rest on the table of contents and §§ 10.05.100 and 3.05.080, consulted for reference only. In paraphrase: § 10.05.100 adopts Title 46.2 of the Code of Virginia by reference (except provisions whose violation is a felony or a Class 1 or 2 misdemeanour), with penalties no greater than under state law. § 3.05.080 assesses $2.00 (courthouse construction and maintenance) and $5.00 (electronic summons system) in each criminal or traffic case charged, $20.00 (courthouse security) in each case ending in conviction, and a $25.00 processing fee for anyone admitted to jail after conviction. eCode360 says its codes may not reflect the latest legislation; the city's official copy was not consulted. No circuit court schedule for non-parallel city traffic ordinances (Va. Code § 16.1-69.40:1(D)) was found.

Costs. No Staunton General District Court prepayment fee sheet was found on vacourts.gov, and the online case system was not opened, so the court's actual cost total for an infraction is not known. Rule 3B:2's total column adds only the $51 processing fee to the fine; its fee-column footnote points to Va. Code §§ 9.1-106 and 53.1-120 for other assessments. Whether the clerk adds the city's $2, $5 and $20 assessments to prepayments, and whether the $5 is charged on tickets written by the State Police (Va. Code § 17.1-279.1 limits it to charges brought by a local law-enforcement agency), was not confirmed. Va. Code § 17.1-281(E), as indexed, says the courthouse assessments are required in each traffic infraction case regardless of a local ordinance.

The 25th Judicial District payment policy (https://www.vacourts.gov/static/online/ppp_fines_costs/dc/staunton.pdf, effective July 1, 2024, dated July 12, 2024) is a scanned image with no text layer. Its quotes here are transcriptions from the page image, which a text search cannot confirm. The Social Security sentence reads 'a Social Security benefit of Social Security Income' in the original (presumably 'or Supplemental Security Income', as in Va. Code § 19.2-354.1(J)); it is quoted as written. The policy covers all General District Courts of the 25th Judicial District, not only Staunton's.

The policy states no payment plan fee. Va. Code § 19.2-354(A) allows a one-time fee of up to $10 when a defendant cannot pay within 90 days of sentencing; whether the Staunton court charges it was not found.

Timing of modifications. The policy says a modification request 'must be made before any default in payments'. Va. Code § 19.2-354.1(H) allows a request 'At any time during the duration of a payment agreement'; after a default the statutory route is a petition for a subsequent agreement (§ 19.2-354.1(I)), which the policy also allows. The policy says the down payment on a subsequent agreement 'will be determined by the amount of the remaining balance' and gives no percentages; the statutory caps are given in fees.

Continuances. The court's page says only 'First continuance granted by Clerk; subsequent requests by Judge on motion.' It does not say whether the clerk's first continuance covers misdemeanour traffic charges (such as reckless driving) or only infractions, or how far the new date may be set; ask the Clerk's Office.

No Staunton court page describes remote hearings or interpreter requests for spoken languages; only the statewide ADA notice in the court pamphlet was found. Interpreter rules (for example Va. Code § 19.2-164) are not covered here.

Magistrate prepayment. Va. Code § 16.1-69.40:1(B) allows the written appearance in person before a magistrate, but the local magistrate office, its hours and the payment methods it takes are not covered here.

Privacy. The court pages name the clerks and judges; no names are recorded here. The phone (540) 332-3878 and fax (540) 332-3985 are the numbers vacourts.gov publishes in the court's contact block with the office hours and address, below the clerk's name, so they are recorded as the Clerk's Office lines; the same applies to the Circuit Court's (540) 332-3874. The Circuit Court page also lists judges' chambers numbers, which were left out. No email address for the General District Court was found.

The Staunton Circuit Court's own payment policy (order of July 1, 2024, https://www.vacourts.gov/static/online/ppp_fines_costs/cc/staunton.pdf; a scan with no text layer) applies to fines and costs owed in that court, for example after an appealed case is decided there. It sets installments of at least $25.00 a month and mentions a 17% collection fee. It is not covered further here, nor are Circuit Court appeal costs, its jury-trial procedure, and the deadline and procedure for an appeal to the Court of Appeals of Virginia.

Prepaying is a conviction on a guilty plea. Va. Code § 16.1-132 allows an appeal within ten days 'whether or not such conviction was upon a plea of guilty', but no Staunton court page says how the ten days are counted after an online or mailed prepayment.

No official Staunton source says whether the court accepts a driver improvement clinic, community service or other terms in exchange for reducing or dismissing a traffic charge. Va. Code § 46.2-505 lets a court require a clinic after a guilty finding, and § 46.2-498 covers voluntary clinics. DMV demerit points, insurance effects and commercial driver's licence rules are not covered here beyond the court pamphlet's statement that DMV assesses points for certain convictions. Va. Code § 46.2-395 (the former licence suspension for unpaid fines and costs) is not in Open US Law's copy of the Code of Virginia, and licence effects of non-payment are not covered here.

Which court. A ticket written in Augusta County goes to the Augusta General District Court (100 Dick Huff Lane, Verona, per its vacourts.gov page), not to Staunton's court, although both are in the 25th Judicial District. This page covers only the Staunton court; Augusta's own pages and policies are not covered here.

Out of scope: Staunton parking tickets (paid to the City Treasurer and contested through the Police Department; see the Staunton parking ticket page), any photo speed or stop-arm camera citations (not covered here), and juvenile traffic cases (Va. Code § 16.1-241, juvenile and domestic relations district court).

The online payment system (eapps.courts.state.va.us) was not opened; the online steps come from the vacourts.gov instructions page. The mail payee 'Staunton General District Court' is inferred from that page's instruction to make the check payable to the applicable district court.

The General District Courts Informational Pamphlet (https://www.vacourts.gov/static/courts/gd/gdinfo.pdf, linked from the court's page) carries a 6/2021 date on its main text and a 10/2024 revision on its ADA notice. The witness-subpoena timing ('at least ten days prior to trial or hearing') comes from Form DC-325 itself.

The index versions of Va. Code §§ 19.2-354 and 19.2-349 are marked effective until January 1, 2027. Their replacement text was not in the index, so the plan-fee, community service and collection rules may change on that date.

eCode360's §§ 10.05.100 and 3.05.080 (its terms bar republishing, not reading) agree with the paraphrases above: § 3.05.080(1) $2.00, (2) $20.00 on conviction, (3) $25.00 jail processing, (4) $5.00. The city's $5.00 text does not itself mention the state limit to charges brought by a local law-enforcement agency (Va. Code § 17.1-279.1).

Rule 3B:2 is a table in the Rules of Court PDF. The residence-district rate ($200 plus $8 per mph) and the § 46.2-820 row ($30, $51, $81) line up only in a layout-mode text extraction of that PDF; the speeding rows ($6 and $7 per mile) also appear in the plain extraction.

Trial in absence. For a traffic infraction, Va. Code § 19.2-258.1 deems the hearing waived and bars a § 46.2-938 warrant; the pamphlet's separate failure-to-appear charge applies to criminal and certain traffic cases. Which misdemeanour traffic charges the Staunton court tries in a defendant's absence is not covered here.

corrections: Quotes: all 104 original quotes were re-checked and confirmed; none needed changing. The 71 state-law quotes are substrings of I.text_of for the cited section (whitespace normalised only), across 23 sections, and each cited subsection letter matches the text. 25 quotes are word for word in the official texts re-fetched on 2026-10-11: the vacourts.gov Staunton GDC page, tickets_dc, the GDC pamphlet and Rule 3B:2 in the Rules of Court PDF. Two Rule 3B:2 quotes containing a section sign match only in a UTF-8 text extraction, and the § 46.2-820 fee row only in layout mode; a caveat notes the table extraction. The 8 quotes from the scanned 25th District payment policy were re-read against the rendered pages and match word for word, including the policy's 'Social Security benefit of Social Security Income'.

Ten state-law quotes added, each checked against I.text_of: § 16.1-69.40:1(A) ('1. Indictable offenses;'), § 46.2-862 (speeds that are reckless driving), § 46.2-868(A) (reckless driving is a Class 1 misdemeanour), § 19.2-353.3 (the clerk may refuse checks or cards on listed grounds), § 19.2-258.1 x4 (judge-only trial of infractions, presumption of innocence, trial in absence with no § 46.2-938 warrant, jury right on appeal) and § 16.1-133 x2 (written notice to withdraw an appeal; affirmance and costs after ten days). lexflow's own check_quotes now reports 81 of 81 code quotes matched and 33 other quotes.

s2: the list of offences that cannot be prepaid left out indictable offences (§ 16.1-69.40:1(A)1) and did not say that speeding 20 mph or more over the limit, or over 85 mph, is reckless driving (§ 46.2-862). Added both, the City Code § 10.05.100 exclusion of felony and Class 1 or 2 misdemeanour provisions, and the § 16.1-69.40:1(D) route for non-parallel city ordinances (no schedule found).

s12: the draft implied any missed traffic case could be tried in absence and lead to a failure-to-appear warrant. For a traffic infraction, § 19.2-258.1 deems the hearing waived, lets the case be heard in absence with notice of the finding, and bars a § 46.2-938 warrant; the pamphlet's separate failure-to-appear charge applies to criminal and certain traffic cases. Fixed; the step's fee now says the $35 cost applies unless good cause is shown at a hearing you request.

s13: 'If your only income is Social Security or SSI ... no payment can be taken from it' merged two rules. Now: under the policy no payment is taken from Social Security or SSI benefits a defendant receives; under § 19.2-354.1(J) a defendant whose sole financial resource is such a benefit is exempt from payments and the case is not sent to collection. 'State law bars a down payment on a first agreement' changed to the statute's wording (the court may not require one; a voluntary one is allowed). Added the § 19.2-354.1(D) installment rule ($25 a month or more by ability to pay, less if indigent). The deadline no longer presents 90 days as a limit on asking for a plan (§ 19.2-354.1(B) requires the court to offer one). Escalation rung 5 now says 'sole financial resource' and covers a referral to collection.

s6: mailing at least 7 days ahead is advice on tickets_dc ('should be mailed'), not a rule; the deadline now says the payment must reach the court before the court date and gives the 7 days as advice.

s7: § 19.2-353.3 says the clerk 'may add' a card fee of up to 4% or a flat fee of up to $2, and may refuse checks or cards on listed grounds. The step said only 'may add a card convenience fee of up to 4%'; both points added and the fee field updated. The returned-check fee amount now says the clerk 'may impose' it, and the card-fee item covers post-court online payments (tickets_dc) and the statutory $2 alternative.

s8: added from § 19.2-266.3 and Form DC-344 that the continuance must be granted in advance, that the form is sworn before a judge, clerk, deputy clerk or notary, and that its instructions send the first copy to the attorney for the Commonwealth (the draft said only that the certificate requires a copy); added from the pamphlet that a judge does not have to grant a continuance request.

s9: 'There is no jury in this court' now rests on § 19.2-258.1 (infractions) and the pamphlet (no jury trials in general district court), with the presumption of innocence added. The ten-day witness subpoena timing is the DC-325 form's advice ('should be filed'), not a rule; reworded in how and deadline. Added the 9:00 am arraignments and advisements docket from the court page.

s17: added the jury right on appeal for a traffic infraction (§ 19.2-258.1), written notice of withdrawal to the court and the prosecution, and that a withdrawal more than ten days after conviction leads the Circuit Court to affirm and tax costs (§ 16.1-133). The DMV sentence is now scoped to the conviction abstract (§ 46.2-383(A)).

Smaller fixes: s1 'goes to' softened to 'is normally returnable to', with the rule to use the court named on the summons. s4 adds the $7 school-crossing and work-zone rate and the residence-district rate ($200 plus $8 per mph) from Rule 3B:2, one fixed fee per incident (§ 16.1-69.48:1(A)) and the pamphlet's statement that the court cannot waive costs; the residence-district fee item now gives that rate and cites the Rule. s5 adds Eastern Time and refunds (tickets_dc). s10 adds that a misdemeanour can carry up to a year in jail (pamphlet) and that reckless driving is a Class 1 misdemeanour (§ 46.2-868(A)). s11 keeps the ADA notice's 'generally, upon request'. s14: the extension request must be received by the Clerk before the due date (policy). s15 adds the policy's definition of default. s16 adds the 4% card fee and the judgment rate (§ 19.2-353.5(D)) and attributes the 181-day interest start to tickets_dc. The Circuit Court address now includes the 2nd Floor shown on its page.

Summary updated (indictable offences and reckless-driving speeds not prepayable, judge-only trial, a plan offered to anyone who cannot pay in full, jury on appeal). Three caveats added (eCode360 re-read, Rule 3B:2 table extraction, trial in absence). Sources added: §§ 19.2-258.1, 46.2-862 and 46.2-868.

Checked and left as they were: the Staunton GDC page facts (hours 8:30 am to 4:30 pm, address, phone, fax, cell phones, docket schedule, continuance policy) and its links to the 25th District policy PDF and the GDC pamphlet; the Circuit Court page (address, Clerk's Office on the third floor, hours 8:30 am to 5:00 pm, Clerk's Office phone, terms beginning the third Monday of January, April, July and October); the Augusta GDC address (100 Dick Huff Lane, Verona; 25th Judicial District); the four form titles against the vacourts.gov traffic and criminal forms lists, with each PDF carrying fillable fields; DC-211's Social Security box; the paraphrases of City Code §§ 10.05.100 and 3.05.080 (read once each on eCode360 for reference, not quoted); every lexflow index row named in sources; and the absence of § 46.2-395 from the index.

Privacy confirmed: no judge, clerk or staff names (the court pages and the policy's signature block name them; none are recorded). The phones are the GDC Clerk's Office line and fax and the Circuit Court Clerk's Office line from vacourts.gov; the Circuit Court judges' chambers lines are left out. No email addresses. Schema: valid JSON in the shape of the other verified place files; step ids s1 to s17 and form ids f1 to f4 are unique, and every step form id exists.
